lines.text: Footwear is one of the most essential parts of any wardrobe. Shoes protect our feet, support our posture, and complete our outfits. The most common everyday shoe is the trainer (British English) or sneaker (American English) — comfortable, cushioned, and perfect for walking, exercise, or casual wear. For formal occasions, men typically wear leather dress shoes or Oxford shoes, while women might choose heels, pumps, or elegant flats. Boots come in many styles: ankle boots are fashionable in autumn, knee-high boots offer warmth in winter, and hiking boots provide grip and ankle support on rough terrain. Wellington boots (wellies) are essential for rain and mud. In summer, sandals, flip-flops, and espadrilles keep feet cool and comfortable. Slippers are the go-to indoor footwear — soft, warm, and cosy for home use. Athletic footwear is designed for specific activities: running shoes have extra cushioning, football boots have studs for grip, and basketball shoes offer ankle support. Understanding shoe vocabulary includes parts of the shoe: the sole (bottom), the heel (back support), the toe (front), the laces (for tying), and the insole (inner cushion). Knowing these terms helps when shopping, discussing fashion, or visiting a cobbler for repairs.

lines.text: 'Trainers' is British English; 'sneakers' is American English. Both refer to casual athletic shoes. In Australia, they're called 'runners' or 'joggers'. Knowing these regional differences helps avoid confusion when shopping abroad.

lines.text: Sneaker collecting is a major cultural phenomenon in English-speaking countries. Limited-edition trainers can sell for thousands. Terms like 'sneakerhead', 'drop' (new release), 'deadstock' (unworn), and 'collab' (collaboration) are common in this subculture.

lines.text: 'Wellies' (Wellington boots) are named after the Duke of Wellington and are iconic in British culture. They're essential for outdoor festivals (like Glastonbury), countryside walks, and rainy weather. Hunter and Barbour are famous brands.
